title: Simulation of Procedure Calls
statement: Let $S$ be a compiler setting, let $d,p,x,k$ be natural numbers, let $[0m\sigma,[0m\sigma'$ be program states, and let $[0m\mathrm{args}$ be a finite list of expressions. Suppose every argument expression is safe in $[0m\sigma$, procedure $p$ has body $[0m\mathrm{body}$ in $S$, and $d$ is less than the depth limit. If $[0m\mathrm{body}$ simulates execution from depth $d+1$ and the state whose variable values are the argument values (with missing arguments set to zero) and whose memory is that of $[0m\sigma$, to $[0m\sigma'$ in $k$ steps, then the call to $p$ with arguments $[0m\mathrm{args}$, assigning its result to variable $x$, simulates execution from $[0m\sigma$ to the state obtained by updating variable $x$ to $[0m\sigma'.[0m\mathrm{loc}(0)$ and using memory $[0m\sigma'.[0m\mathrm{mem}$, in $[0m\sum_{e\in\mathrm{args}}\mathrm{cost}(e)+2+k$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: Every argument expression is safe in the initial state
Procedure p is defined with body body in the setting
The current depth is below the depth limit
The body simulates from depth d+1, with the argument frame and initial memory, to the given state in k steps
replaced:
Let $S$ be a program setting, and consider a call to procedure $p$ with argument
expressions $\mathrm{args}$, assigning the returned value to local variable $x$, from
state $\sigma$ at depth $d$. Suppose every argument expression is safe in $\sigma$,
procedure $p$ has body $\mathrm{body}$ in $S$, and $d$ is less than the depth limit. If
executing that body at depth $d+1$, from the state whose locals are the argument values
(with missing arguments taken to be zero) and whose memory is $\sigma.\mathrm{mem}$,
simulates execution to $\sigma'$ in $k$ steps, then the call simulates execution to the
state obtained by assigning $\sigma'.\mathrm{loc}(0)$ to local $x$ and using memory
$\sigma'.\mathrm{mem}$, in $(\sum_{e\in\mathrm{args}}\mathrm{cost}(e))+2+k$ steps.
